text: Hello. My name is Richard Smith, and I'm
the senior director of data and
accountability for Portland Public
Schools.
In this video, I'll give you a better
idea of how our district got to the
point of discussing school
consolidations and closures.
The key issue is a steady decline in
enrollment that is causing some
elementary, K-8, and middle schools to
be seriously under-enrolled and
under-resourced.
This decline has been happening over the
past decade, and is due to several
factors beyond our control.
These factors include a declining birth
rate,
families moving out of Portland, and
parents making other educational choices
for their children.
Under-enrolment makes it challenging to
provide the robust programming that our
students need and deserve.
Let me give you an example.
Elementary School A has an enrollment of
350 students, while Elementary School B
has 200 students. School A can provide
full-time art and PE teachers, while
School B can only support part-time art
and PE teachers.
Class sizes also may be uneven at the
two schools. For example, a fourth-grade
teacher at School A may have a full
class of 30 students, and a fourth-grade
teacher at School B may only have 14
students.
In the right-sizing process, we can
consolidate them into one school with
550 students.
That would allow all students have
full-time art and PE teachers and
fourth-grade classes of 22 students
each.
Also, keeping all of our current schools
open would be unsustainable financially.
That's because our district receives
funding based on the number of students
enrolled.
So, lower enrollment means less funding
in the future.
That's on top of cuts we already made at
the start of this school year. And a
significant funding shortfall in the
coming year.
Taken all together, we must take action
now to make PPS more stable and
sustainable for the future of our
students. Thank you.
